    Covariate balance before and after weighting

    Source: R/causal-balance.R
    epi_balance.Rd

    Computes standardized mean differences (SMDs) between binary exposure groups for numeric covariates and indicators for each observed factor or logical level. Both unweighted and weighted SMDs use the same denominator: the square root of the mean of the two unweighted sample variances within exposure groups. The numerator is the exposed mean minus the unexposed mean, before or after separate group normalization of weights. Using a fixed denominator helps avoid apparent balance improvements caused only by changing weighted variance.

    Usage

    epi_balance(.data, exposure, covariates, weights = NULL)

    Arguments

    .data

    An ungrouped data frame of individual observations.

    exposure

    Binary 0/1 exposure column.

    covariates

    Tidy selection of complete numeric, factor or logical covariate columns. Factor and logical variables expand to level indicators.

    weights

    Optional non-negative numeric weight column. Defaults to equal weights; each exposure group must have positive total weight.

    Value

    A tibble with covariate, level (NA for numeric variables), unweighted and weighted group means, fixed reference standard deviation and unweighted and weighted SMDs. Exposure 1 minus exposure 0 defines the sign.

    Details

    SMDs are descriptive diagnostics, not tests of exchangeability, positivity, correct model specification or causal validity. They do not diagnose balance of interactions or nonlinear transformations unless supplied as columns, and there is no universally sufficient threshold. Undefined SMDs caused by a zero pooled standard deviation are NA; this may indicate severe non-overlap.

    Examples

    d <- data.frame(e = c(0, 0, 1, 1), age = c(20, 30, 30, 40), w = c(1, 2, 2, 1))
epi_balance(d, e, age, weights = w)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 9
#>   covariate level mean_unexposed mean_exposed weighted_mean_unexposed
#>   <chr>     <chr>          <dbl>        <dbl>                   <dbl>
#> 1 age       NA                25           35                    26.7
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: weighted_mean_exposed <dbl>, reference_sd <dbl>,
#> #   smd_unweighted <dbl>, smd_weighted <dbl>
